newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Five die after drinking varnish in Romanian prison.
newsitem.headline: Five die after drinking varnish in Romanian prison.

text.p: Five inmates of a Romanian prison died after drinking varnish containing methylated spirits from a furniture factory where they performed rehabilitation work, officials said on Monday.

The head of Gherla prison in central Romania told state television 48 men had been taken to hospital after inmates working at the factory inside the prison walls smuggled out the varnish and distributed it to comrades. Five died later.
Vasile Muresan said the varnish was stolen last Wednesday when guards and inmates were absorbed with international soccer matches on television.
"They used a system called the carriage," he told the television. "One prisoner used a rope to lower a bag from a window overlooking the factory, the bottles were placed inside and then hoisted out."

Sixteen inmates have been released from hospitals in the nearby city of Cluj after recovering from the effects of the varnish. Television quoted doctors as saying they could still lose their eyesight.
The head of the factory, a lieutenant-colonel, and 19 other military officers running it were dismissed in connection with the incident.
Methylated spirits is alcohol for industrial uses, mixed with highly poisonous methanol to render it undrinkable. It is nonetheless drunk by some resulting eventually in death.
